rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so this candidate raises obfuscation pressure across the board. The binary is tiny (684 text bytes, 2 functions) so size overhead is nearly free; the dominant constraint is the hot FP loop in main, hence moderate RuntimeCost weights for BCF and FLA so the control-flow flattening and bogus-control-flow passes are applied but not maximally aggressive on the loop body. SUB and FLA get the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain since arithmetic substitution and flattening give the best static-analysis resistance per unit cost on dense numeric code; SPLIT stays low-cost/low-gain as a cheap complement that aids FLA; IBR adds indirect dispatch to frustrate basic-block-level recovery; ICALL and IGV hide call targets and global values, which matters little for a 2-function binary but adds symbolic/noise barriers cheaply; CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low everywhere since round 0 showed no stability issues, leaving headroom to push further if this round also passes.
